name: sql-qa
description: Six questions over the package's own Chinook copy, graded by execution accuracy: two single-table counts, one one-join aggregation, one two-join revenue question, one whose true answer is zero, and one the database cannot answer. The zero case is a third category beside answerable and refusal — the database can answer it, and the answer is none (launch-readiness/172). The point of the fixture is that this is the only example in the twenty whose expectation is a machine's, not a reader's — the answer is graded by re-executing the SQL the run stated, not by matching its prose. Expected rows come from scripts/refresh_eval_expectations.py, never from a hand.

cases.question: How many customers are in the database?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer
cases.notes: The catalogue's own smoke question. 59 is the figure a reader can check by hand.

cases.question: How many albums are in the database?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS AlbumCount FROM Album
cases.notes: A second single-table count, on a table the first question gives no reason to look at — sql_list_tables has to be read, not remembered.

cases.question: Which genre has the most tracks? Give the genre name and the number of tracks.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT g.Name AS Genre, COUNT(t.TrackId) AS TrackCount FROM Genre g JOIN Track t ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId GROUP BY g.GenreId, g.Name ORDER BY TrackCount DESC LIMIT 1
cases.notes: One join, and the join rule is a foreign key sql_get_table_schema reports. The ORDER BY picks the row rather than presenting it, so ordering is not graded.

cases.question: Which country's customers have spent the most in total? Name the country and the total.
cases.gold_sql: SELECT c.Country, ROUND(SUM(i.Total), 2) AS Spend FROM Customer c JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId GROUP BY c.Country ORDER BY Spend DESC LIMIT 1
cases.notes: Two tables and a rounded sum. Billing country lives on Invoice as well, so a run that joins the wrong way round gets a different figure — which is what execution accuracy is for.

cases.question: How many customers are from Antarctica?
cases.gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS CustomerCount FROM Customer WHERE Country = 'Antarctica'
cases.notes: An answerable question whose answer is none. Country is a real column with real values and Antarctica is not one of them, so this is neither a refusal (s05, a column that does not exist) nor a miss — the query is right and the count is zero. Added by launch-readiness/172: the shipped example answered this with the digit 0 and no noun, and a dataset with no zero case had nothing to fail against on the path a new user runs first.

cases.question: What is each customer's date of birth?
cases.notes: Chinook records no birth dates. The honest run reads the Customer schema, finds no such column and says so; a run that produces dates produced them from nowhere.
